subject: Ninety-nine of a hundred cities, and the same air
alt: Sandeep Adhwaryu's cartoon: the grey sky is thick with thousands of specks of black soot and dust. At the upper left a white and blue helicopter is flying, and the speech bubble from it says in English: I'M NOT SURE IF WE CAN BUILD VIKSIT BHARAT ONLINE, SIR. Below is a large government building of red-brown stone, its high dome coated in soot; a small pavilion sits on top of the dome, smaller domes flank it below, and the long wall in front has small square windows. The masthead at the top reads TOI LINE OF NO CONTROL, SANDEEP ADHWARYU, and beneath it the headline: 99 OF WORLD'S 100 MOST POLLUTED CITIES ARE IN INDIA. The cartoonist's signature is at the lower left.
chutki: The Times of India headline says that ninety-nine of the world's hundred most polluted cities are in India. In the cartoon the helicopter flies through that same poisoned air, and a voice from inside says it is not sure whether 'Viksit Bharat' can be built online.

Adhwaryu's barb cuts both ways. On one side is the 2047 dream of a developed India, on the other the air in which it is hard to breathe. Where nobody can stand outside, the country will have to be built 'online'. The soot on the dome says that even the highest office of power sits in the same smoke, and the ash on the wall in front questions every claim of a clean-up.
